binomial-cdf.name: Binomial CDF Calculator
binomial-cdf.intro: Enter the number of trials n, success probability p and upper bound x to get the cumulative probability P(X<=x) of a binomial distribution, for acceptance sampling, reliability and cumulative binomial analysis.

binomial-pmf.name: Binomial PMF Calculator
binomial-pmf.intro: Enter trials n, success count k and success probability p to compute the probability of exactly k successes in n independent Bernoulli trials, for discrete distributions and risk modelling.

chi-square-test.name: Chi-Square Test Calculator
chi-square-test.intro: Enter observed and expected frequencies to compute the chi-square statistic and judge whether the deviation is significant, for goodness-of-fit and independence tests.

coefficient-of-variation.name: Coefficient of Variation Calculator
coefficient-of-variation.intro: Enter the mean and standard deviation to compute CV = sigma/mu x 100%, comparing dispersion across data sets measured in different units.

cohens-d.name: Cohen's d Effect Size Calculator
cohens-d.intro: Enter two group means and pooled standard deviation (or group SDs and sizes) to compute Cohen's d and measure effect size for comparing experimental results.

confidence-proportion.name: Proportion Confidence Interval Calculator
confidence-proportion.intro: Enter the number of successes and sample size (or the sample proportion) to get the confidence interval for a population proportion by normal approximation, for surveys and medical estimation.

correlation-coefficient.name: Pearson Correlation Coefficient Calculator
correlation-coefficient.intro: Enter paired X and Y data to compute the Pearson correlation coefficient r, measuring the strength and direction of a linear relationship, with a significance check.

correlation-r-squared.name: Coefficient of Determination (R-squared) Calculator
correlation-r-squared.intro: Enter the correlation coefficient r to compute the coefficient of determination R-squared, the share of variance in the dependent variable explained by a regression model.

cramers-v.name: Cramer's V Calculator
cramers-v.intro: From the chi-square value, sample size and degrees of freedom of a contingency table, compute Cramer's V to measure the association strength between two categorical variables.

f-test-variance.name: F-Test for Equal Variances Calculator
f-test-variance.intro: Enter two sample variances and their degrees of freedom to compute the F statistic and critical value and test whether two population variances are equal.

geometric-mean.name: Geometric Mean Calculator
geometric-mean.intro: Enter a set of positive numbers to compute the geometric mean as the n-th root of their product, suited to growth rates and ratio-type data.

harmonic-mean.name: Harmonic Mean Calculator
harmonic-mean.intro: Enter a set of numbers to compute the harmonic mean as the reciprocal of the arithmetic mean of reciprocals, suited to rates and unit prices.

independent-t-test.name: Independent Two-Sample t-Test Calculator
independent-t-test.intro: Enter two independent samples (means, standard deviations and sizes) to compute the t value and p value and test whether the two population means differ significantly.

iqr.name: Interquartile Range (IQR) Calculator
iqr.intro: Enter a data set (or count, minimum, Q1, median, Q3 and maximum) to compute Q1, Q2, Q3 and the interquartile range, and mark outlier bounds by the 1.5 x IQR rule for box plots.

linear-regression.name: Least-Squares Linear Regression Calculator
linear-regression.intro: Enter paired (x, y) data to fit the best-fit line by least squares and get the slope, intercept and R-squared, for trend prediction and variable-relationship modelling.

mean-absolute-deviation.name: Mean Absolute Deviation (MAD) Calculator
mean-absolute-deviation.intro: Enter a series of values to compute the mean absolute deviation MAD = sum|x - xbar| / n, measuring average dispersion for forecast error and robustness checks.

normal-cdf.name: Standard Normal CDF Calculator
normal-cdf.intro: Enter the mean, standard deviation and a value x, or a standard score z, to compute the standard normal cumulative probability P(X <= x) for probability and quantile estimates.

odds-ratio.name: Odds Ratio Calculator
odds-ratio.intro: Enter the four frequencies of a 2x2 contingency table to compute the odds ratio and its confidence interval, measuring exposure-outcome association in epidemiology.

one-sample-t-test.name: One-Sample t-Test Calculator
one-sample-t-test.intro: Enter sample data (or mean, standard deviation and size) to test a sample mean against a hypothesised population mean when the population SD is unknown, returning t, df and p.

one-sample-z-test.name: One-Sample z-Test Calculator
one-sample-z-test.intro: Enter the sample mean, sample size and known population standard deviation to test the sample mean against a hypothesised value, returning the z statistic and one/two-sided p values.

one-way-anova.name: One-Way ANOVA Calculator
one-way-anova.intro: Enter two or more group means, standard deviations and sizes to compute between-group and within-group sums of squares, the F value and p value for one-way analysis of variance.

p.name: P-Value from z-Score Estimator
p.intro: Enter a z statistic to approximate the two-sided p value using the normal distribution, with a note that p below 0.05 usually rejects the null hypothesis at the 5% level.

paired-t-test.name: Paired t-Test Calculator
paired-t-test.intro: Enter paired measurements of the same subjects (e.g. before and after treatment) to compute the mean and SD of differences and test whether the difference is non-zero, returning t, df and p.

percentile-rank.name: Percentile Rank Calculator
percentile-rank.intro: Enter a data set and a target value to compute the percentile rank, i.e. the percentage of the data below that value, for score and ranking evaluation.

poisson-pmf.name: Poisson PMF Calculator
poisson-pmf.intro: Enter the average event rate lambda per unit time or space and the target count k to compute the Poisson probability mass P(X=k), for rare-event modelling such as call arrivals or failures.

pooled-variance.name: Pooled Variance Calculator
pooled-variance.intro: Enter two sample sizes and standard deviations to compute the pooled variance as a weighted average, used for the equal-variance assumption before a two-sample t-test.

population-variance.name: Population Variance Calculator
population-variance.intro: Enter a complete data set to compute the population variance as the average squared deviation from the mean, measuring dispersion with results computed locally.

probability-complement.name: Complementary Probability Calculator
probability-complement.intro: Enter the probability of an event p to compute the complementary probability P(Ac) = 1 - P(A), a basic probability operation.

range-stat.name: Range Calculator
range-stat.intro: Enter a series of values to compute the range R = max - min, a quick measure of the spread of a data set.

relative-risk.name: Relative Risk (RR) Calculator
relative-risk.intro: Enter the outcome rates of an exposed and an unexposed group to compute the relative risk RR and its confidence interval, measuring exposure-outcome association in cohort studies.

sample-size-mean.name: Sample Size for Estimating a Mean
sample-size-mean.intro: Given a confidence level, margin of error and population standard deviation, estimate the minimum sample size needed to estimate a population mean, for experiment design.

sample-size-proportion.name: Sample Size for Estimating a Proportion
sample-size-proportion.intro: Given a confidence level, margin of error and expected proportion, estimate the minimum sample size needed to estimate a population proportion, for survey design.

sample-variance.name: Sample Variance Calculator
sample-variance.intro: Enter a data set to compute the sample variance using n - 1 degrees of freedom, measuring dispersion for inferential statistics and hypothesis testing.

skewness-sample.name: Sample Skewness Calculator
skewness-sample.intro: Enter a series of values to compute the sample skewness g1 from the third standardised central moment, judging left/right skew and symmetry of a distribution.

standard-error.name: Standard Error of the Mean Calculator
standard-error.intro: Enter the sample standard deviation and sample size to compute the standard error of the mean SE = s / sqrt(n), used in confidence intervals and significance tests.

standard-error-proportion.name: Standard Error of a Proportion Calculator
standard-error-proportion.intro: Enter the sample proportion p and sample size n to compute SE = sqrt[p(1-p)/n], the sampling variability of a proportion estimate, for proportion confidence intervals and tests.

statistics.name: Normal Distribution Probability Calculator
statistics.intro: Enter the mean, standard deviation and lower/upper bounds to compute the probability (area under the normal curve) for that interval, useful for cumulative probabilities and quantile ranges.

statistics-10.name: Coefficient of Variation Comparison
statistics-10.intro: Enter the mean and standard deviation of two data sets to compare their coefficients of variation CV, removing the effect of units when comparing dispersion.

statistics-11.name: Weighted Mean Calculator
statistics-11.intro: Enter values together with their weights to compute a weighted mean with automatic weight normalisation, for weighted scores and indicators.

statistics-12.name: Mean, Median and Mode Calculator
statistics-12.intro: Enter up to seven values to quickly compute the arithmetic mean, median, mode and range and the total, a fast way to describe central tendency and spread of a data set.

statistics-13.name: Standard Deviation and Variance Calculator
statistics-13.intro: Enter a set of values and choose sample or population to compute standard deviation, variance and the coefficient of variation, comparing dispersion across different units.

statistics-16.name: Linear Regression Fit Calculator
statistics-16.intro: Enter paired (x, y) sample data to fit the line y = ax + b by least squares, output the slope a, intercept b, correlation and goodness of fit, and predict y for any x.

statistics-4.name: Confidence Interval for a Mean Calculator
statistics-4.intro: Enter the sample mean, standard deviation, sample size and a confidence level (e.g. 95%) to estimate the confidence interval for the population mean with a z value, for large samples or known population SD.

statistics-5.name: Sample Size Estimator
statistics-5.intro: Enter the acceptable margin of error, confidence level and population standard deviation to estimate the minimum sample size for a mean, planning sample counts with sufficient precision.

statistics-7.name: Skewness and Kurtosis Calculator
statistics-7.intro: Enter a data set to compute skewness and kurtosis and judge whether the distribution is left- or right-skewed and more peaked or flatter than normal, spotting tail features.

stddev-list.name: Sample Standard Deviation Calculator
stddev-list.intro: Enter a comma- or space-separated list of numbers to compute the sample standard deviation s with n - 1 denominator, assessing how spread out the observations are.

t.name: One-Sample t Statistic Calculator
t.intro: Enter the sample mean, hypothesised population mean, sample standard deviation and sample size to compute the one-sample t statistic (xbar - mu)/(s/sqrt(n)) and its degrees of freedom.

t-score.name: t-Statistic Calculator
t-score.intro: Enter the sample mean, hypothesised mean, standard deviation and sample size to compute the t statistic for a mean hypothesis test.

variance-list.name: Sample Variance Calculator (Data List)
variance-list.intro: Enter a comma- or space-separated list of numbers to compute the sample variance s2 = sum(x - xbar)2 / (n - 1), the squared standard deviation used in statistical description and ANOVA.

z.name: Z-Score Calculator (with Percentile)
z.intro: Enter a raw score, population mean and population standard deviation to standardise the score as z = (x - mu)/sigma and get its percentile rank, comparing values across distributions.

z-score-calc.name: Z-Score Calculator
z-score-calc.intro: Enter a raw value, mean and standard deviation to compute the z score (x - mu)/sigma, for standardisation and outlier detection.
